what: Repeating over many simulated data sets
title: Benchmarking factor methods
text: small benchmark loop, varying signal strength:
code: bench_one <- function(effect, seed) {   s <- simulate_multiomics(n_samples = 45, effect = effect, seed = seed)   r <- run_factor_pipeline(s$data, methods = c("PCA", "MFA", "JIVE"), k = 3,                            verbose = FALSE)   cl <- cluster_results(r, k = 3, include_data = FALSE)   out <- compare_clusterings(cl, setNames(s$metadata$group,                                           s$metadata$sample))$vs_truth   out$effect <- effect   out } grid <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(1, 1.5, 2, 3), function(e)   do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(sd) bench_one(e, sd))))) agg <- aggregate(ARI ~ method + effect, grid, mean) library(ggplot2) ggplot(agg, aes(effect, ARI, colour = method)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2) +   scale_colour_manual(values = factomics_palette(3)) +   labs(x = "Group effect size", y = "Mean ARI (3 replicates)",        title = "Group recovery as signal increases") +   theme_factomics()

title: Methods and how to tune them
text: default (scale_features = TRUE) every feature z-scored, features start footing, zero-variance features set zero. Samples aligned across views name. data already normalised way want, use scale_features = FALSE.

title: Methods and how to tune them
text: simplest integrative baseline: views stacked single PCA run. pca_block_weight = TRUE (default) view divided square root number features, view 10,000 genes swamp view 50 metabolites. needs nothing beyond base R.
code: res_pca <- run_factor_pipeline(sim$data, methods = "PCA", k = 4,                                verbose = FALSE) round(res_pca$PCA$meta$variance_percent, 1) #> [1] 16.6 13.9  8.8  2.7

title: Methods and how to tune them
text: MFA (FactoMineR) weights view first eigenvalue, runs global PCA. fast, deterministic strong default. needs least two views. mfa_group_sizes can override grouping columns.

title: Methods and how to tune them
text: FABIA sparse, biclustering-oriented factor model: factor driven small set features subset samples. fabia_alpha controls loading sparseness (larger = sparser), fabia_cyc number iterations.
code: res_fabia <- run_factor_pipeline(sim$data, methods = "FABIA", k = 4,                                  fabia_alpha = 0.05, fabia_cyc = 500,                                  verbose = FALSE)

title: Methods and how to tune them
text: GFA Bayesian factor model view-wise sparsity: factor can active views, , one. gfa_iter_burnin gfa_iter_max control Gibbs sampler. iterations give stable factors.
